headline: Nepali Army calls its Bhotekoshi flood rescue 'incomparable, historic and exemplary'
dek: The army says seven people were pulled alive from buried hydropower tunnels, even as disaster officials count 1,453 dead and 5,285 still missing a month on.
body_markdown:
The Nepali Army has ruled its own performance in the Rasuwa Bhotekoshi flood disaster "incomparable, historic, and exemplary." The verdict appears in a report the army released on September 27, one month after the August 26 flood buried roads, bridges, and hydropower tunnels along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers.

The report singles out one chapter as the hardest of the whole response: pulling survivors out of hydropower tunnels choked with mud and boulders. The army says seven people came out alive from those buried tunnels, including two rescued on September 5 after crews cut through the tunnel's arched crown to reach them. DC Nepal, OnlineKhabar and Ratopati carried the report on September 27, and Ratopati's English edition confirms the same figures and language.

The army lists the conditions its teams worked under: weather that shifted fast and without warning, narrow mountain flight corridors, too few helipads, communication lines cut, a river whose flow no one could predict, landslides that kept falling, and tunnels packed with debris. A video described by the Kathmandu Post showed one soldier pulling a trapped worker through thick mud inside a tunnel while another pushed him from behind.

## A rescue measured against a heavy toll

The army's self-praise sits inside a much larger and grimmer count. By August 30, four days into the disaster, the army said it had rescued 2,697 people, 2,497 of them by helicopter including 216 foreign nationals, and the rest on foot. More than 8,300 soldiers were deployed, the army told the Kathmandu Post.

By September 26, Nepal's disaster authority, the NDRRMA, put the toll far higher across the whole flood, not just the tunnels: 1,453 dead and 5,285 still missing, according to Nepal Press. The same report says 13,795 people have been rescued overall, with more than 20,000 police, army, and armed police personnel mobilized. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha told Parliament on September 23 that more than 800 hydropower workers alone remained unaccounted for, a figure that has come down only slowly since it topped 900 in early September, the Kathmandu Post reported. OnlineKhabar reports the army's figure of 2,798 people rescued from the hydropower area overall. The seven are those freed from tunnels later packed with mud and boulders. Seven people pulled alive from buried tunnels is a real achievement. It is also a small number next to the more than 800 hydropower workers the minister says are still unaccounted for.

## Recovery still slow, a month on

Nepal Press's own reporting on the one month mark shows why "historic" success sits uneasily next to daily hardship. Road links to Rasuwa remain broken. The army has built a temporary bridge at Devighat in Nuwakot, and the roughly ten kilometre Bidur to Betrawati stretch has reopened for the most part, but the route from Devighat to Parika village still needs a tuin, a cable pulley crossing, because no bridge stands there yet. A 72 metre bailey bridge is being prepared for Betrawati. Nagarik News reported on September 26 that the collapse of Rasuwa's road network has caused food shortages and made it hard for poorer residents to reach medical treatment.

Efforts to reopen the Rasuwagadhi trade route to China before the Dashain festival are underway, led by the Department of Roads, the army, and a government task force, Ratopati reported. Until that route reopens and permanent bridges replace bailey crossings, families displaced by the flood will keep depending on temporary shelter, rented rooms, and relief deliveries that Nepal Press says are still ongoing a month after the water hit.

social_hook: The army calls its flood rescue historic. A month later, disaster officials say 5,285 people are still missing.
take: The army graded its own flood response and gave itself top marks. Seven people pulled alive from buried tunnels is real. So is the rest of the ledger: 1,453 dead, 5,285 missing, and more than 800 hydropower workers unaccounted for by the Energy Minister's own count. Rasuwa's roads are still broken and one village link is a cable pulley. A month on, historic is a word for later.

nepali.headline: सेनाले आफ्नो उद्धारलाई "ऐतिहासिक" भन्यो, ५,२८५ अझै बेपत्ता
nepali.dek: सेनाका अनुसार पुरिएका सुरुङबाट सात जना जीवितै निकालिए, तर विपद् प्राधिकरणका अनुसार एक महिनामा १,४५३ जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ र ५,२८५ जना अझै बेपत्ता छन्।
nepali.take: सेनाले आफ्नो उद्धारको मूल्याङ्कन आफैं गर्‍यो र आफ्नै पिठ्युँ थपथपायो। सुरुङभित्र पुरिएका सात जना जीवितै निकालिएको कुरा सत्य हो। बाँकी लेखा पनि उत्तिकै सत्य छ, १,४५३ जनाको मृत्यु, ५,२८५ जना बेपत्ता र ऊर्जामन्त्रीकै भनाइमा ८०० भन्दा बढी जलविद्युत कामदारको अत्तोपत्तो छैन। रसुवाका सडक अझै भत्किएका छन् र एउटा गाउँको सम्पर्क अझै तुइनमै सीमित छ। एक महिनापछि पनि यस्तो अवस्था छ भने
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । नेपाली सेनाले रसुवाको भोटेकोशी बाढी उद्धारमा आफ्नो भूमिकालाई "अतुलनीय, ऐतिहासिक र अनुकरणीय" भनेको छ। सेनाले आइतबार (२७ सेप्टेम्बर) सार्वजनिक गरेको प्रतिवेदनमा यस्तो लेखिएको छ। २६ अगस्टको बाढीले भोटेकोशी र त्रिशूली नदी किनारका सडक, पुल र जलविद्युत सुरुङ पुरेको थियो। त्यसको एक महिनापछि यो प्रतिवेदन आएको हो।

प्रतिवेदनले हिलो र ढुङ्गामाटोले पुरिएका जलविद्युत सुरुङभित्रबाट मानिस निकाल्ने कामलाई सम्पूर्ण उद्धार अभियानकै सबैभन्दा कठिन अध्याय भनेको छ। सेनाका अनुसार त्यस्ता पुरिएका सुरुङहरूबाट सात जना जीवितै निकालिए। तीमध्ये दुई जनालाई उद्धार टोलीले ५ सेप्टेम्बरमा सुरुङको माथिल्लो घुमाउरो भाग काटेर निकालेको थियो। डीसी नेपाल, अनलाइनखबर र रातोपातीले आइतबार यो प्रतिवेदनबारे समाचार छापेका छन्। रातोपातीको अंग्रेजी संस्करणमा पनि उही तथ्याङ्क र शब्द छन्।

सेनाका अनुसार उद्धार टोलीहरूले कठिन अवस्थामा काम गरे। मौसम अचानक फेरिन्थ्यो, पहाडी हवाई बाटो साँघुरो थियो र हेलिप्याड अपुग थिए। सञ्चार अवरुद्ध थियो, नदीको बहाव अनुमान गर्न सकिँदैनथ्यो, पहिरो खसिरहन्थ्यो र सुरुङ मलबेले भरिएका थिए। द काठमाडौं पोस्टले वर्णन गरेको एउटा भिडियोमा एक सैनिकले सुरुङभित्र हिलोमा फसेको कामदारलाई तानिरहेको र अर्को सैनिकले पछाडिबाट धकेलिरहेको देखिन्छ।

## भारी क्षतिबीच उद्धार

तर सेनाले आफैंलाई दिएको यो प्रशंसा बाढीको धेरै ठूलो र कठोर क्षतिको बीचमा आएको छ। ३० अगस्टसम्म, बाढी आएको चार दिनभित्रै, सेनाले २,६९७ जनालाई उद्धार गरेको बताएको थियो। तीमध्ये २,४९७ जना हेलिकप्टरबाट निकालिएका थिए, जसमा २१६ विदेशी नागरिक थिए। बाँकी पैदल मार्गबाट निकालिएका थिए। सेनाले ८,३०० भन्दा बढी सैनिक परिचालन गरेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टलाई बताएको थियो।

नेपाल प्रेसका अनुसार राष्ट्रिय विपद् जोखिम न्यूनीकरण तथा व्यवस्थापन प्राधिकरणले २६ सेप्टेम्बरसम्म बाढीमा १,४५३ जनाको मृत्यु भएको र ५,२८५ जना अझै बेपत्ता रहेको जनाएको छ। यो तथ्याङ्क सुरुङको मात्र होइन, सम्पूर्ण बाढीको हो। सोही प्रतिवेदनअनुसार समग्रमा १३,७९५ जना उद्धार भइसकेका छन्। २० हजारभन्दा बढी प्रहरी, सेना र सशस्त्र प्रहरी परिचालन गरिएको छ।

ऊर्जामन्त्री विराजभक्त श्रेष्ठले २३ सेप्टेम्बरमा संसदमा ८०० भन्दा बढी जलविद्युत कामदार अझै बेपत्ता रहेको बताएका थिए। यो सङ्ख्या सेप्टेम्बरको सुरुतिर ९०० नाघेकोदेखि बिस्तारै मात्र घटेको हो, द काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। अनलाइनखबरका अनुसार सेनाले जलविद्युत क्षेत्रबाट समग्रमा २,७९८ जना उद्धार गरेको दाबी गरेको छ। यो सङ्ख्या सुरुङबाट जीवितै निकालिएका सात जनाभन्दा फरक हो। ती सात जना चाहिँ पछि हिलो र ढुङ्गामाटोले भरिएका सुरुङभित्रबाट जीवितै निकालिएका हुन्। यसरी सुरुङबाट जीवितै फर्किनु वास्तविक उपलब्धि हो। तर ऊर्जामन्त्रीले नै अझै ८०० भन्दा बढी जलविद्युत कामदार बेपत्ता रहेको बताउँदा यो सङ्ख्या सानो देखिन्छ।

## एक महिनापछि पनि सुस्त पुनर्निर्माण

एक महिना पुगेको अवसरमा नेपाल प्रेसले छापेको समाचारले "ऐतिहासिक" सफलता र दैनिक कष्टबीचको दूरी देखाउँछ। रसुवा जोड्ने सडक अझै भत्किएकै छन्। सेनाले नुवाकोटको देवीघाटमा अस्थायी पुल बनाएको छ। करिब १० किलोमिटर लामो बिदुरदेखि बेत्रावतीसम्मको सडक खण्ड धेरैजसो पुनः खुलेको छ। तर देवीघाटदेखि पारिका गाउँसम्मको मार्गमा अझै तुइनकै भर पर्नुपरेको छ, किनभने त्यहाँ अझै पुल बनेको छैन। बेत्रावतीमा राख्न ७२ मिटर लामो बेली पुल तयार हुँदैछ। रसुवाको सडक सञ्जाल भत्किँदा खाद्य अभाव भएको र गरिब बासिन्दालाई उपचार पाउन कठिन भएको नागरिक न्यूजले शनिबार (२६ सेप्टेम्बर) जनाएको छ।

दशैंअघि रसुवागढी नाकाको व्यापार मार्ग पुनः खोल्ने प्रयास जारी छ। यसको नेतृत्व सडक विभाग, सेना र सरकारी कार्यदलले गरिरहेका छन्, रातोपातीले जनाएको छ। नाका नखुलेसम्म र बेली पुलको ठाउँमा स्थायी पुल नबनेसम्म विस्थापित परिवार अस्थायी आवास, भाडाको कोठा र राहतमै भर पर्नेछन्। नेपाल प्रेसका अनुसार बाढी आएको एक महिनापछि पनि राहत वितरण जारी छ।

नेपाली सेनाले भोटेकोशी बाढी उद्धारलाई आफैं "अतुलनीय, ऐतिहासिक र अनुकरणीय" भनेको छ। सेनाका अनुसार हिलो र ढुङ्गामाटोले पुरिएका जलविद्युत सुरुङहरूबाट सात जना जीवितै निकालिए, जसमा दुई जनालाई सुरुङको माथिल्लो भाग काटेरै ५ सेप्टेम्बरमा बचाइयो।

nepali.notes: सम्पादकले दिएका दस वटै सुधार तिनका ठाउँमा लागू गरियो (शीर्षकको वाक्य क्रम, दुई ठाउँमा कर्तावाच्य सच्याइयो, टोलीले र निकाल्ने कामको विवरण, सुरुङका सात जनासम्बन्धी वाक्य, उपशीर्षक, बेत्रावती पुलको वाक्य, र क्याप्सनको नागरिक न्यूज वाक्य)। सुधारपछि उही अनुच्छेदमा 'सात जना' दोहोरिएकोले प्रवाहका लागि एउटा वाक्यलाई 'यसरी सुरुङबाट जीवितै फर्किनु वास्तविक उपलब्धि हो' भनी सामान्य रूपमा मिलाइयो, तथ्य वा श्रोत नबदली। कुनै तथ्य, नाम, संख्या वा उद्धरण हटाइएको छैन।
nepali.editor: Two sentences distort the record: one invents a comparison with an army 'claim' of damage, and one moves 'later' from the tunnels to the rescue. The caption also overstates Nagarik's report, and several sentences carry English order or passive voice that need rewriting.

ranking.reason: Today's only new fact is the Nepali Army's self-assessment of its Rasuwa Bhotekoshi response. It is publishable only as an attributed institutional claim. It must be paired with Nepal Press's slow-recovery report and the unresolved toll of dead and missing, so it does not read as army PR.

Confirmed at rank 3 with conditions. It is publishable as an attributed Nepali Army claim, balanced by Nepal Press's slow-recovery report, which sits in the story's own source cluster. The balance therefore does not depend on unverified outside material.

findings.passage: Soldiers featured in widely shared video pulling a worker through the mud by hand while another pushed from behind.
findings.problem: This closely paraphrases a specific video description from a Kathmandu Post story published August 29, 2026 ("Hundreds feared trapped in hydropower tunnels after Bhotekoshi flood"), which says soldiers were "working through thick, frozen mud inside a tunnel, with one soldier pulling a trapped worker while another pushes him from behind." That Kathmandu Post story is not in the sources list, so this claim has no traceable, named source in the article as house style requires. It also risks being an uncredited close paraphrase of another outlet's original reporting.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the Kathmandu Post August 29 story to the sources list and attribute the video description to it explicitly, e.g. 'a video described by the Kathmandu Post showed soldiers pulling a worker through mud while another pushed from behind,' or drop the sentence if it cannot be sourced.

findings.passage: The verdict appears in a report the army released through the state news agency RSS on September 27
findings.problem: None of the four cited sources for this claim (Ratopati English, OnlineKhabar, DC Nepal, Ratopati Nepali) say the army distributed its report through RSS. This detail about the distribution channel appears to be invented rather than traced to a named source, which the house rules explicitly forbid.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the reference to RSS unless a source confirming that distribution channel is added to the sources list. Simply say the army released the report, citing the outlets that carried it.

findings.passage: including two rescued on September 5 after crews cut through the tunnel's arched crown to reach them
findings.problem: CNN reported that two men were pulled alive from a hydropower tunnel 'nine days after floods' that struck on August 26, which lands on September 4, not September 5. The article does not flag or reconcile this one day discrepancy between CNN and the army's own account carried by Ratopati, even though house style requires reporting disagreements between outlets.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the original army report and CNN's dateline, and either reconcile the date or add a line noting CNN reported the rescue a day earlier, on September 4.

findings.passage: seven survivors pulled from tunnels is a real achievement and also a small fraction of who went in
findings.problem: OnlineKhabar's own report on the army's conclusion cites a much larger figure, 2,798 people, rescued from the hydropower tunnel area overall, with the seven referring specifically to people freed from tunnels later choked with mud and boulders. The article never mentions the 2,798 figure, so readers cannot judge whether 'seven' is being fairly measured against the true scale of the tunnel rescue effort or is being used to make the army's self assessment look thinner than the full record supports.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the 2,798 figure for total people rescued from the hydropower tunnel area, distinguishing it clearly from the seven rescued from tunnels that were later buried by mud and rock, so the comparison to missing workers is apples to apples.

findings.passage: The army's self-praise sits inside a much larger and grimmer count.
findings.problem: Calling the army's own assessment 'self-praise' is an editorial characterization of a public institution's official statement. It is defensible as fair comment given the data that follows, but it edges close to loaded language rather than the neutral, fact-forward tone the house style otherwise favors, and could be read as the outlet taking a side rather than reporting a contrast.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the juxtaposition of numbers make the point. Replace 'self-praise' with a neutral framing such as 'The army's assessment sits inside a much larger and grimmer count.'

findings.problem: The story object's own headline translates the same Nepali phrase as 'historic and unparalleled,' while this article renders it as 'incomparable, historic, and exemplary.' The underlying Nepali (per OnlineKhabar) is closer to three separate words, atulniya, aitihasik, anukaraniya, so the article's three word rendering is more literal, but the inconsistency across the pipeline's own outputs on the same quote should be resolved so the outlet is not seen quoting the same statement two different ways.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize the translated quote across the story summary and the article body so the same three word rendering is used everywhere.

findings.passage: The Nepali Army calls its Rasuwa flood response historic. A month on, disaster officials still count 1,453 dead and 5,285 missing.
findings.problem: This social hook buries the sharpest angle, the tension between an institution's self-praise and an unresolved death toll, behind flat, list-like phrasing. It reads as a summary rather than a hook and does not carry the payload the headline promises.
findings.suggested_fix: Sharpen to something like: 'The army calls its flood rescue historic. A month later, 5,285 people are still missing.' to make the contrast land in one breath.

findings.passage: Three Nepali outlets, DC Nepal, OnlineKhabar, and Ratopati, carried the report within the same hour on September 27
findings.problem: This detail about publication timing across outlets is process trivia for a reader in Nepal or the diaspora. It does not advance the story and takes up space that could go to the missing 2,798 figure or a clearer reconciliation of the toll numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut this sentence or shorten it to a passing attribution clause, and use the freed space for substantive context readers need.

red_team.summary: The article is well sourced overall and correctly juxtaposes the army's self assessment against a grim toll, but it invents or under sources two details, the RSS distribution claim and the video description that closely mirrors an uncredited Kathmandu Post story. It also omits a key figure, 2,798 people rescued from the tunnel area overall, that would let readers properly judge the seven survivor figure, and it misses a one day date conflict with CNN's reporting on the tunnel rescue. The story is timely and relevant to Nepal and diaspora readers, its structure follows house style, but the hook and social copy underplay the sharpest angle and the accuracy gaps need fixing before publication.

responses.response: The video detail is not covered by any source currently in our list. Even if we saw the footage independently, the specific phrasing ('pulling... while another pushed from behind') tracks too closely to the Kathmandu Post's original description. We need either that outlet in our sources with attribution, or we drop the detail.
responses.proposed_edit: Add 'The Kathmandu Post, https://kathmandupost.com/national/2026/08/29/hundreds-feared-trapped-in-hydropower-tunnels-after-bhotekoshi-flood' to the sources list, used for the video description. Rewrite the sentence as: 'A video described by the Kathmandu Post showed a soldier pulling a trapped worker through the mud while another pushed from behind.'

responses.response: We checked the Ratopati English piece directly and it does not mention RSS as the distribution channel for the army's report. None of our four cited outlets say that. This detail was not traceable and should not have been asserted.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the sentence to: 'The verdict appears in a report the army released on September 27, one month after the August 26 flood buried roads, bridges, and hydropower tunnels along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers.' Drop the RSS reference entirely unless a source naming RSS as the distributor is added.

responses.response: The September 5 date comes from the army's own report, which is our primary source here and is corroborated independently by three Nepali outlets (DC Nepal, OnlineKhabar, Ratopati) plus Ratopati's English edition, all published the same hour. CNN is not in our sources list and its September 3 dispatch describing 'nine days after' the flood is itself an approximation, not a dated confirmation from the army. We are faithfully reporting what the entity making the claim, the army, says about its own rescue timeline. Bringing in an uncited outlet to manufacture a discrepancy risks introducing an unverified claim of our own.
responses.proposed_edit: No change to the article text. If we want extra rigor, we could independently verify the September 5 date against the army's original press statement before next publication cycle, but this does not require an edit to the current piece.

responses.response: OnlineKhabar's report on the army's own conclusion gives a broader total of 2,798 rescued from the tunnel area, distinct from the seven pulled from tunnels that were later buried by mud and rock. Without that larger figure, our line about 'a small fraction' compares seven against total missing hydropower workers rather than against the fuller tunnel rescue effort, which is not an apples to apples comparison.
responses.proposed_edit: Add a clause: 'The army's report says 2,798 people were rescued from the wider hydropower tunnel area overall; the seven figure refers specifically to survivors freed from tunnels that collapsed and were later buried in mud and boulders. Set against more than 800 hydropower workers still unaccounted for as of September 23, both figures show a rescue effort still short of the scale of the loss.'

responses.response: Self-praise is a plain description of what happened: the army wrote a report calling its own performance 'incomparable, historic, and exemplary' and released it. That is not spin, it is an accurate label for an institution assessing itself, and house style asks us to take a position when facts support one rather than hedge. The sentence is immediately followed by hard numbers that let the reader judge for themselves, so the framing does not substitute opinion for fact.

The finding describes a mismatch between the article's headline and body, but in the version we published both the headline and the body use the identical three word rendering, 'incomparable, historic and exemplary.' There is no inconsistency in this draft to fix. If the finding is pointing at an older or different version of the story summary, that document is not part of what we are defending here.
responses.proposed_edit: No change needed. If a separate story summary elsewhere on the site uses different wording, that summary should be updated to match this article, not the other way around.

responses.response: The suggested rewrite is sharper and keeps the same two facts, the army's self-assessment and the missing count, while landing the contrast faster. This is a reasonable tightening with no loss of accuracy.
responses.proposed_edit: Change social_hook to: 'The army calls its flood rescue historic. A month later, 5,285 people are still missing.'

responses.response: The same-hour publication detail across three outlets is useful for showing this was a coordinated release rather than an exclusive, which has some value for media literate readers, but it is a minor point next to the missing 2,798 figure and toll reconciliation we are adding elsewhere. Trimming it frees space without losing anything essential.
responses.proposed_edit: Shorten to: 'DC Nepal, OnlineKhabar, and Ratopati carried the report on September 27, and Ratopati's English edition confirms the same figures and language.'

defense.summary: We accept five of eight findings. Two are genuine sourcing failures that need fixing before republication: the RSS distribution claim, which no cited source supports, and the tunnel rescue video description, which closely tracks the Kathmandu Post's original phrasing without credit. We also accept the missing 2,798 total rescued figure, which sharpens an unfair comparison, and two low stakes tightening suggestions for the social hook and a trims of publication timing detail. We contest three findings: the September 5 rescue date is well corroborated across our own primary sources and does not need reconciling against an uncited CNN dispatch; 'self-praise' is accurate description, not loaded language, and is immediately grounded in numbers; and the claimed headline versus body inconsistency does not exist in the version we are defending, since both use the same three word translation.

rulings.note: The video description and the words 'widely shared' trace to no listed source. The sentence closely tracks the Kathmandu Post's August 29 wording without credit. It must be attributed or cut.
No cited outlet names RSS as the channel for the army report. That is an untraceable detail in the lede. Remove it.

The article already attributes the September 5 date to the army. CNN's 'nine days after' is a day count in a live blog, not a dated confirmation, and CNN is not a source here. No edit is required, but the editor should keep the date inside the army's attribution.

The core problem is 'a small fraction of who went in'. No source gives how many people went into the tunnels, so that comparison is unsupported. The 2,798 figure needs care. It sits close to the army's overall total of 2,697 by August 30, so the editor must use OnlineKhabar's exact wording for what it counts. The defence's proposed text also adds 'collapsed' and uses a banned semicolon.
'Self-praise' is fair comment on an institution grading its own work. The numbers that follow it immediately back it up, and house style asks the piece to take a position when facts support one.
The headline and body use the same three word rendering. The only difference is a serial comma. The story summary is outside this article.
The sharper hook is better. Its version drops the attribution on the missing count, so that attribution must be kept.
'Within the same hour' is process trivia and cannot be easily verified. Shorten it to a plain attribution.

One editing pass fixes all three, along with the hook and trim edits, after which the piece should clear the accuracy and defensibility targets.
